name: Rio Grande do Sul floods and Porto Alegre flood-defence failure
place: Rio Grande do Sul state; central Porto Alegre
operator: DMAE (Porto Alegre municipal water and drainage utility)
deaths: 185 confirmed by the state Defesa Civil (Aug 2025), plus 23 missing. Earlier counts were 177 (June 2024) and 182 to 184. No official source gives exactly 183.
affected: About 2.4 million residents in 478 of 497 state municipalities. In Porto Alegre, the city's own figures say 30% of the territory, 160,000 people and 93,000 homes were affected. Other counts are lower (see figures).
damage: Gates without maintenance leaked and pumping stations stopped, so central Porto Alegre could not drain. DMAE said 11 of 23 pumps were running and 19 stopped at the peak because of flooding or electrical faults. The Guaiba peaked at 5.37 m on 5 May 2024, against 4.76 m in 1941.
legal_outcome: No charges reported. State prosecutors (MPRS) are handling procedures. On 18 Sep 2024 the city and DMAE presented recovery plans for pump houses, gates and dikes. A city council inquiry (CPI) produced split reports. The mayor denies a maintenance failure.
summary: Floods hit most of Rio Grande do Sul in May 2024. In Porto Alegre, the flood-defence system run by the municipal utility DMAE failed. Critics blame missing maintenance. The mayor says the 1968 design was never built for a flood this size. The company was never privatized.

operator: Eletronorte system (Manaus Energia manages the dam)

deaths: No death toll for 1987-89 found. The Waimiri-Atroari population fell from about 3,000 in the 1970s to 332 in the 1980s (about 89%, Brasil de Fato citing CNV); FUNAI estimates give about 80% between 1972 and 1986. CNV counts 2,650 deaths; the Amazonas Truth Committee about 2,000. One source argues the BR-174 highway and military action, not Balbina, caused this. Contested.

legal_outcome: MPF (Amazonas) filed an action seeking R$ 50 million over the Waimiri-Atroari genocide (IHU, Aug 2017). Outcome not found.
summary: Balbina flooded about 2,360 km2 of Amazon forest and part of Waimiri-Atroari land. It produced little power for its size. Hundreds of families got no compensation. The Waimiri-Atroari population collapsed over the same period; how much is due to the dam is disputed.
